overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the chair may limit public speaking, audio problems at the August 31, 2016 meeting did not amount to a violation, and other allegations were declined as non-OML issues.

allegations.summary: Chair allowed one audience member to speak but declined others at a August 31, 2016 meeting, allegedly regulating public participation unfairly.
allegations.key_passage: While we find that it is within the chair's discretion to limit participation, and thus the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law with respect to this allegation, we encourage public bodies to allow public participation during meetings whenever possible.

allegations.summary: Board discussion at the August 31, 2016 meeting was allegedly inaudible to members of the audience, denying meaningful access to the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because of this, we find that any audio problems did not rise to the level of an Open Meeting Law violation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board did not sufficiently discuss a piece of business, lacked due diligence, created a hostile atmosphere, and voted unwisely; AG declined review.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, these allegations do not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

allegations.summary: Request for further review questioned how the Board responded to the complaint; AG clarified the 14-day review and remedial-action procedure, though not a pleaded allegation.
allegations.key_passage: The body must review the complaint before authorizing legal counsel, or any other individual, to respond on its behalf.
